title: 7-round AES-192: Conditional-table complete-key claim

target.description: Reduced-round AES-192 with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted. The source's key-search stages and whole-key headline are separated.Step8 proposes exhaustive search for remaining key material. The source's headline budgets do not separately itemize that completion; later literature disputes the running-time analysis.

setting.key_relation: Fixed standard AES key schedule; component derivations treat its round-key bytes as constants, not as a related-key oracle.
setting.key_population: General key under the source's modeled internal-parameter events; no special master-key class is specified.
setting.plaintext_model: 2^48 structures of2^32 plaintexts varying the four diagonal bytes; under a guessed first-round key they split into2^72 active-byte sets. Matching uses33 inputs/32 differences, or65 inputs/64 differences for eight rounds.
assumptions: Probabilities for internal parameters use the paper's randomness assumptions; they are not independently established for all AES keys.

Step3 andStep4 each enumerate2^40 partial-key guesses over2^80 blocks. The source's2^113 figure prices these partial-decryption/encryption passes; the joint Step5–6 matching and Step8 completion are not separately costed.
The source treats2^8 partial encryptions/decryptions as one encryption and four byte-function evaluations as one seven-round encryption. These are source conventions, not independent calibration.
The conditional15-parameter table must use the corrected substitution; printed Equation9 has a coefficient discrepancy.
DKS2010 disputes the cost analysis. The original claim is retained with no normalized running-time exponent.

time.reported: 2^113 claimed; DKS10 says running time is about2^32 greater
time.note: Original online claim and later critique remain distinct. No corrected end-to-end encryption exponent is certified here.

data.note: 2^48 diagonal structures of2^32 blocks. Eight-round extension retains this data count.

memory.note: Two precomputed target-function tables; eight rounds double the sequence length. Complete online lookup/storage accounting remains under review.

preprocessing.note: Reusable key-independent table. Source convention uses approximately four function evaluations per seven-round encryption; no replacement work calibration is inferred.

success.description: Section4.2 states approximately50% success for its average-case seven-round attack figures. This is the original author claim; formulas and running-time analysis have documented discrepancies.

evidence.locator: Printed pp.150–152 Section4.2 Steps1–8, complexity/success paragraph and p.154 Table1
evidence.interpretation: Complete official proceedings read and critical page images checked. Original claims remain attributed to DTCB09; later objections have their own source-specific observations.
Raw-first complete inventory and independent component review completed; source costs and whole-attack reproduction remain separate.

limitations: Formal component tests and author-reported budgets are distinct from an end-to-end attack reproduction.
The2^-136 false-match heuristic for32-byte sequences is not an end-to-end success probability. Sixty-four-byte matching is a distinct extension.
Later DKS10 correction observations are attached through field_conflicts with their own source and locator; they are not attributed to the original DTCB09 authors.

field_conflicts.label: Reduced Equation9 coefficient
field_conflicts.description: Under Equation7's conditions, substituting c12=3*d1 into corrected Equation4 gives coefficient1 for S(3*x1+3*d1). Printed Equation9 instead uses coefficient3. The conditional15-parameter count survives the corrected substitution; literal precomputation values differ.

observations.locator: Printed p.148 Equation4 and p.149 Equation7
observations.reported: The last term of C3_22 is S(3*x1+c12); c12=3*d1 leaves coefficient1.
The corresponding reduced term is printed as 3*S(3*x1+3*d1).

field_conflicts.label: Later running-time objection
field_conflicts.description: DKS2010 explicitly disputes DTCB2009's cost analysis and its sub-exhaustive AES-128 conclusion. Preserve the original2^113 claim and the later about2^32 factor without certifying a corrected end-to-end exponent.

observations.locator: Printed pp.151–152 Section4.2 and p.154 Table1
observations.reported: Online attack complexity is claimed as2^113 encryption equivalents.
The authors state that DTCB09's analysis is flawed, its running time is about2^32 greater than claimed, and it exceeds exhaustive search for AES-128.

observations.locator: Printed pp.420–421 AppendixA, matching Steps5–6 analysis
observations.reported: AppendixA explicitly counts the omitted joint matching as at least2^40×2^40×2^80=2^160 operations; these are not encryption units.
